investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never started, blocking the entire remote-agents feature eval surface.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never reaches a running state, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) never completes createAgent(), so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all concurrently running or pending remote agent pods have consumed the full VM slot allocation on the 2 kata-capable nodes, leaving zero capacity for new pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective schedulable pool is permanently limited to those 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, no scheduling is possible regardless of cluster size.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote agent VMs not releasing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: prior eval runs or user-created agents may not have been cleaned up, holding VM resource slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain held.

Lower confidence — transient cluster event (node drain, rolling update, resource pressure) temporarily reduced available kata-capable nodes from a higher baseline to 2, coinciding with the eval run window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable by the Kubernetes scheduler: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never started, blocking the entire remote-agents feature eval surface.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never reaches a running state, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) never completes createAgent(), so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remain absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) is fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent provisioning was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM never reached a schedulable state and the eval runner never received any runtime response.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place remote agent pods on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or allocatable count at zero), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the createAgent call in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never completed, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a full contract violation. This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
